key_insight: A hybrid quantum-classical method reconstructs spin-system energy degeneracies from imaginary-temperature partition functions measured with a single ancilla qubit.
engineering_relevance: The approach enables quantum-assisted thermodynamic calculations, with circuit optimizations tailored to commuting spin interactions.
method: Measure the partition function at imaginary inverse temperatures using one ancilla qubit.
Apply an inverse discrete Fourier transform on a known, equally spaced energy grid to recover degeneracies.
Optimize circuits using commuting interactions and Eulerian ordering.
evidence_signal: Tests on periodic Kagome Ising antiferromagnets with up to 36 spins on ibm_kingston retained dominant spectral features and reproduced the main temperature dependence of exact heat capacities.
watch_item: Exact reconstruction requires a known, equally spaced energy grid and noiseless measurements; substantial circuit depth and hardware noise limit practical accuracy.
paper_title: Quantum computation of energy level degeneracy and thermodynamical properties of spin systems
